messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick update — starting 2026-08-01 we're rolling out two PTO policy changes: (1) monthly pro-rata accrual instead of front-loaded annual buckets, and (2) a new 40-hour rollover buffer (up from 32) to reduce forced encashment. See details below and a short FAQ link.

Ava (People Ops): TL;DR: more predictable accrual for new hires and fewer people losing days at year-end. We'll run a one-time reconciliation for current balances on 2026-07-31.

Liam (Finance): Note: the one-time reconciliation may trigger a taxable encashment for accruals above the new cap if people don't choose rollover or use the hours. We'll publish examples in the FAQ.

Jon (Eng): Will this apply to contractors or only full-time headcount?

Maya (People Ops): Good question — contractors and vendors are unchanged. This only affects Redwood employees on payroll.

Diego (Design): Any change to how managers approve PSTO? (we sometimes have people pre-booking big blocks)

Ava (People Ops): Approvals stay in the same flow. Managers will see the updated balance in the PTO UI; pre-booked future time is respected and won't be reclaimed by reconciliation.

Jon (Eng): Cool. Is there an opt-out window for people who prefer annual front-loading?

Maya (People Ops): Not broadly — we found monthly pro-rata better for equity across hires. If someone has a documented business reason (e.g., long-term secondment), they can file a case with People Ops and Finance; we'll review exceptions.

Liam (Finance): We'll also add a small UI flag for payroll to mark any one-time encashment as "voluntary" vs "required" to help with tax handling.

Priya (HR-bot): FAQ & policy doc: https://intranet.redwood/workplace/policies/pto-accrual-rollover-buffer-2026 (also posted in #docs).

Diego (Design): Thanks — this should help folks plan. Any comms to managers + heads so teams can synchronize?

Maya (People Ops): Yes — we're sending a manager brief next week with sample emails and suggested talking points for team meetings. Also a short AMA drop-in on 2026-07-15 16:00 UTC.

Jon (Eng): :thumbsup:  Will the PTO export for headcount/people analytics change shape? I use the CSV for planning.

Ava (People Ops): Slightly. The CSV will include new fields: accrual_period_start, accrual_rate_per_month, and rollover_buffer_hours. We'll keep the old columns for backward compatibility for one quarter.

Maya (People Ops): Action items: 1) People Ops to publish final FAQ by 2026-07-01, 2) Payroll runs reconciliation 2026-07-31, 3) Manager brief and AMA on 2026-07-15. If you have edge cases DM me or post here.

Liam (Finance): Ping me if you want sample payroll numbers for your teams — happy to help.

Diego (Design): Thanks, team.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks all — feel free to drop questions here; we'll update the FAQ as we go. :sparkles:
